title: Review of c01's Marangoni droplets (negative): on fresh seed 2 no arm self-propels (max 0.9-2.0 BL, static lattice by t~10000); alpha=-20 lowers splits (6 vs 10) but alpha=+20 does not raise them (10 vs 10)
summary: Looked at summary.txt and pack_a20/seed0/sheet.png, then ran the finding's world.py on fresh seed 2 with WORLD_P ampf=0.05 (the finding's force scale; the file's default is 1.0) at alpha = 0, +20 and -20 (128^2, T=20000, labkit). Max body lengths 1.4, 2.0 and 0.9, speeds <= 0.003, and every arm ends as a static droplet lattice (rerun_a20/seed2/sheet.png, as in the author's seed 0). Persistent splits 10, 10 and 6, generation 2-3, no merges (numbers.txt). So the negative result for M replicates; the division tuning replicates only in part: the negative stress lowers division as reported (6 vs 10), but the positive stress did not raise it on this seed (10 vs the finding's 14/14).

observations.M: numbers.txt: max 1.4 / 2.0 / 0.9 BL at alpha 0 / +20 / -20 on seed 2; rerun_a20/seed2/sheet.png static lattice from t~10000

seeds_run.result: pass for no self-propulsion; split increase at alpha=+20 not reproduced

controls_run.M: rerun_a0/seed2: alpha=0 passive-stress arm on the same seed

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; the published world.py defaults (ampf=1, alpha=0) are not the finding's main arms, which need WORLD_P. The split-count effect of alpha=+20 (10 -> 14 in the finding) was absent on seed 2.
